Citing unnamed U.S. officials, Bloomberg reported that Moscow and Washington were discussing economic cooperation in the far north, which could "drive a wedge" between Russia and key trading ally China. It could also be part of a detente between the U.S. and Russia sought by U.S. President Donald Trump.
Newsweek reached out to the U.S. State Department and the Russian Foreign Ministry for comment.

The Pentagon's new Arctic Strategy, released last year, highlighted the risk of China and Russia teaming up in the Arctic. The Biden-era policy sought to expand its military readiness and surveillance in the region.
